finding.claim: A form body whose Content-Type carries parameters (e.g. 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8') is never parsed by default, so ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY stay empty and body rules do not see the payload.
finding.source: Request Content-Type header, attacker-controlled, with parameters appended.
finding.sink: AddRequestHeader sets reqbodyProcessor only on exact match; ProcessRequestBody returns early at the rbp=="" branch with no body variables populated.

trace.note: AddRequestHeader content-type case compares full lowercased value to exact string
URLENCODED only set on exact match; no parameter stripping
ForceRequestBodyVariable defaults false (waf.go:210), so no forcing
rbp empty: rules evaluated with no body parsing

finding.guards_checked: ForceRequestBodyVariable default off; no parameter stripping in AddRequestHeader; CRS-style phase-1 ctl:requestBodyProcessor rules would mitigate (not verified in repo).

finding.claim: @inspectFile fails open: any exec error (including E2BIG for oversize argv, timeout, non-zero exit) returns no-match, so a deny rule does not fire.
finding.source: Request value (e.g. REQUEST_BODY) passed as argv to the operator-configured program.
finding.sink: exec.CommandContext(ctx, o.path, value).CombinedOutput(); error path returns false.

trace.note: err != nil or deadline exceeded returns false (no match)

finding.guards_checked: No shell involved (argv form). Behavior on exec failure inferred from Go/OS semantics; not run.

finding.claim: When url.ParseRequestURI fails, query arguments and QUERY_STRING are never extracted, so payloads in the query evade ARGS/QUERY_STRING rules.
finding.source: Request line target, attacker-controlled, e.g. GET /%zz?x=<payload>.
finding.sink: ProcessURI error branch skips ExtractGetArguments and leaves query empty; only REQUEST_URI/REQUEST_LINE carry the raw payload.

trace.note: error branch sets urlencodedError and requestURI only
queryString set from empty query on error path

finding.guards_checked: URLENCODED_ERROR is set; effectiveness depends on rules alerting on it or on REQUEST_URI matches. Backend acceptance of malformed path assumed, not verified.

finding.claim: ArgumentLimit silently drops GET args beyond the limit (evasion), and is not enforced on body arg paths, letting a single request create unbounded post args (memory DoS).
finding.source: Query string (GET) for the evasion case; urlencoded/multipart/JSON body for the resource case, attacker-controlled.
finding.sink: AddGetRequestArgument skips args over limit; urlencoded.go:28-30, multipart.go:109, json.go:34-35 write args directly with no limit.

trace.note: GET args dropped once Len() >= ArgumentLimit (default 1000, waf.go:348)
body args written via argsCol.Set with no limit
default RequestBodyLimit 128 MiB when body access enabled

finding.guards_checked: Silent skip logged at debug only; no alert rule. Body limit applies to byte size, not arg count.

finding.claim: On any non-EOF XML decode error, readXML discards all values already collected and the processor returns without populating RequestXML, so a payload placed before a malformed tag is not inspected.
finding.sink: readXML returns nil,nil,err; ProcessRequest returns early, leaving RequestXML empty.

trace.note: non-EOF error returns nil,nil,err, dropping attrs and content
ProcessRequest returns err without populating RequestXML
contrast: JSON populates best-effort args before returning error

finding.guards_checked: REQBODY_ERROR is set and rules still evaluate; impact depends on rule set blocking on REQBODY_ERROR.
